sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
இன்னல் அகல நேர்வழி இயம்புவேன் கேளீர்
மின்னல் நிகர்மேனி மாதவன் என்றே
sections.translit:
innal agala nErvazhi iyambuvEn kELIr
minnal nigarmEni mAdhavan endRE
sections.en: Listen to my message, folks. The only path to solve your suffering is to worship Lord Madhava whose dazzling form is like lightning.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
மிகுந்த வலியோ அம்மா இதமாய் அணைத்தே
உகந்த மருந்தும் தந்துப் பரிவாய்ப் பாடிடுவேன்
அஞ்சனமும் தீட்டி அழகானப் பட்டுடுத்து
மஞ்சளும் எழிலூட்ட வண்ணமலர் மணங்கூட்ட
ஶ்ரீதரன் மணக்கோலம் காணவே விரைந்திடும்
தோழியர் குழாம் ஒன்றின் பவனி கண்டேன்
கார் குழலார் சூழக் களியொடு கோயில் சென்று
பார் ஏத்தும் பரமனை வைதேகி மருங்கினில்
சீர் மறை ஓதும் வேதியர் முழக்கொடு பரவிப் பின்
ஆர்வொடு கடுகி வரும் வரை சிறிதே உறங்குமின்
குடை நிழலிருந்து குஞ்சரம் ஊர்ந்த நாள் போய்
பருந்துக்கு விருந்தாகும் பாழ் உடல் கெட்டு
தொற்று வியாதியும் சற்றும் கண் படாது வருத்தும்
புற்று நோயும் முற்றிய காலை வற்றிய உன் நிலை சகிப்பார் எவரே
தவறும் செய்தேனோ தனிமை இழந்தேனோ
கவரும் இளமையும் வீணழித்தேனோ அடாது இவ்வெண்ணம்
மனிதர் சேவை மகேசன் சேவை அல்லவா
புனிதமான இப்பணி அன்னை தெரீசா பாதை அல்லவா
sections.translit:
migundha valiyO ammA idhamAy aNaitthE
ugandha marundhum thandhup parivAyp pAdiduvEn
Charanam 1
anjanamum thItti azhagAnap pattudutthu
manjaLum ezhilUtta vaNNamalar maNangkUtta
srIdharan maNakkOlam kANavE viraindhidum
thOzhiyar kuzhAm ondRin bhavani kaNdEn
Charanam 2
kAr kuzhalAr sUzhak kaLiyodu kOyil sendRu
pAr Etthum paramanai vaidEgi marunginil
sIr maRai Odhum vEdhiyar muzhakkodu paravip pin
Arvodu kadugi varum varai siRidhE uRangumin
Charanam 3
kudai nizhalirundhu kunjaram Urndha nAL pOy
parundhukku virundhAgum pAzh udal kettu
thotRu vyAdhiyum satRum kaN padAdhu varutthum
putRu nOyum mutRiya kAlai vatRiya un nilai sagippAr evarE
Charanam 4
thavaRum seydhEnO thanimai izhandhEnO
kavarum iLamaiyum vINazhitthEnO adAdhu ivveNNam
manidhar sEvai magEsan sEvai allavA
punidhamAna ippaNi annai therIsA pAdhai allavA
sections.en: Dear mother, are you having too much pain? I will give you your medicine on time. I will hug you and sing you a soothing song to comfort you. Charanam 1 I just saw the procession of my girlfriends. They have applied mascara to their eyelashes and the turmeric paste applied on their body is adding charm to these looks.They are dressed up beautifully with silk saris and wearing colorful fragrant flowers on their tresses. They are rushing to see the wedding of Vishnu and Lakshmi at the temple. Charanam 2 I will go in the company of my youthful friends to the temple. I will see the Lord being worshipped all over the world with his consort Vaidehi. I will briefly watch their spectacular wedding celebration, replete with Vedic chanting. As soon as it is done, I will rush back to my duties. Mother dear, please relax and take a nap until I get back. Charanam 3 What luxury this woman must have had in her life!  Perhaps she is used to riding an elephant, with a canopy offering her shelter from the heat and rain. Those days are gone. Her body has suffered deterioration, infested with contagious diseases and now by the invisible cancer. She has become fragile and needs assistance for her daily chores. She has lost considerable weight.Who would tolerate this transformation? Charanam 4 Have I made a serious mistake in pursuing this profession? Have I lost quality time? Have I wasted my charming youth? No, I should not entertain such bad thoughts. Is it not true that service to humanity is service to the Almighty? Have I not chosen this sacred profession with a goal to follow the path of Mother Theresa?

notes:
This song was written for Smt. Jayanthi Sridharan, Artistic Director of Bharathakala Kutiram, San Jose, CA, for a program held as a fundraiser for the Adyar Cancer Institute in Chennai, India.
The song is narrated from the perspective of a young woman who serves as a caretaker for cancer patients. She experiences a whirlwind of emotions as she watches her friends enjoying life — going to a Sridharan (Vishnu) wedding with Vaidegi (Lakshmi) at a nearby temple, dressed in silk saris, adorned with gold jewelry, and wearing makeup.
In the next moment, her sense of duty calls out to her. She tells her patient that she will hug her gently, administer necessary medicine on time, and sing a soothing song to comfort her. Yet a part of her wonders if she might sneak away for a few minutes — just long enough to witness the divine wedding and return quickly. She hopes the patient might rest or take a short nap until she’s back.
She reflects on the patient’s condition: perhaps this woman was once wealthy and vibrant, her health gradually deteriorating, her body succumbing to decay, disease, and eventually cancer. As the illness took over, she became fragile and completely dependent on others for even the simplest of tasks. Who could bear such a heartbreaking transformation?
The caretaker then turns inward, contemplating her own life. Has she made a mistake choosing this path? Has she sacrificed her personal time and the golden years of her youth in this demanding profession?
But ultimately, her sense of purpose prevails. She resolves to cast aside such negative thoughts. "Is it not true," she says, "that service to mankind is service to the Almighty?" After all, was it not her sacred calling to follow in the footsteps of Mother Teresa?
